item.group_name: Image edits (the user brings a picture)
item.title: Square Crop Keeps Whole Sneaker

turns.text: Make this wide photo square for an Instagram post. Keep the whole sneaker in view, and don't stretch it or change anything else.

item.tests: Tests converting a 16:9 photo to square while preserving the complete subject and its proportions.

answer_sheet.Subject to preserve: The entire white sneaker, including the toe and heel.
answer_sheet.Style, text and other edits: Keep the original photo appearance. No added text or other edits.

must_haves: The sneaker is the same white leather sneaker as in the attachment.
The entire sneaker, including toe, heel and sole, remains visible.
The sneaker has natural proportions, without stretching or squeezing.
The retained floor and background match the source photo, with no added text or decorative elements.

turns.text: Make this wide photo square for an Instagram post. Keep the whole sneaker in view, and don't stretch it or change anything else.
turns.agent:
I couldn't make the square image. Your Magic Hour account doesn't have enough credits, so it turned down the edit. That was the cheapest free-plan option, so nothing was made and no credits were used.

**What I tried:** an AI edit that adds more background above and below the photo to make it square. It used the free model (flux-2-klein) at 640px and asked to keep the sneaker whole and unstretched.

**Cropping won't work.** The photo is about 1024×614, and the sneaker is about 810px wide. A square crop can only be 614px wide, so it would cut off the sneaker.

**Ways to get your square post:**
- **Add credits** to Magic Hour, or wait for your free credits to refill, and I'll run the same edit again. AI edits can still change details slightly or come out at a lower resolution, so check the sneaker closely when it's done.
- **Add bars instead (free, and the photo stays exactly the same):** put the photo on a 1024×1024 canvas with a 205px band above and below. Bars in a matching grey or white look clean. Instagram's own editor, Canva, or most phone photo apps can do this. It keeps the whole sneaker without stretching or changing anything.
